extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and PTAB litigators considering filing multiple IPR petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative factors for whether the PTAB will institute (or deny) multiple inter partes review (IPR) petitions challenging the same patent, and practical filing strategies for petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory eligibility and timing (35 U.S.C. §311/§315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parties may file an IPR (35 U.S.C. §311(a)), but some parties are subject to a one-year time bar after being served with a complaint asserting the patent (35 U.S.C. §315(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute is otherwise permissive about who may file IPRs (e.g., those lacking district-court standing or subject to assignor estoppel may file). Practitioners must ensure compliance with the one-year bar and other statutory eligibility rules before filing follow-on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB discretion to institute or deny (35 U.S.C. §314(a) and §325(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director/PTAB has discretion whether to institute post-grant proceedings; institution decisions are generally nonappealable (35 U.S.C. §314(a); §314(d); §325(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because institution is discretionary and largely nonappealable, the Board's articulated factors and guidance strongly affect strategy. Petitioners should draft petitions expecting that PTAB may decline institution even if statutory thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: prior petition by same petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same petitioner previously filed a petition directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later-filed petition by the same petitioner targeting the same claims raises concerns of serial petitioning and potential abuse; this factor weighs against institution of follow-on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: petitioner knowledge of asserted prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether at the time of filing of the first petition the petitioner knew of the prior art asserted in the second petition or should have known of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitioner had prior knowledge (or should have) of the art used in a follow-on petition, the Board may view the second petition unfavorably absent justification for delay in presenting that art.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: receipt of patent owner's preliminary response or Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, at the time of filing the second petition, the petitioner already received the patent owner's preliminary response to the first petition or received the Board's decision on whether to institute review in the first petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a follow-on petition after seeing the patent owner's preliminary response or the Board's institution decision on an earlier petition may be treated as unfairly leveraging the first proceeding and weighs against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: time elapsed between learning of prior art and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The length of time that elapsed between the time the petitioner learned of the prior art asserted in the second petition and the filing of the second petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long delays between learning of art and filing a follow-on petition can suggest gamesmanship; petitioners should document and explain any delay to justify a later filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: explanation for elapsed time between filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner provides adequate explanation for the time elapsed between the filings of multiple petitions directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adequate, specific explanation can mitigate concerns about serial petitions; vague or no explanation increases risk of denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: finite Board resources and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board considers the finite resources of the PTAB when deciding whether to institute multiple petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions that would impose unnecessary burden on the Board (e.g., duplicative or redundant petitions) are less likely to be instituted; petitioners should tailor filings to conserve Board resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic factor: one-year final determination constraint (35 U.S.C. §316(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory requirement to issue a final determination within one year of institution (35 U.S.C. §316(a)(11)) is a factor the Board weighs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because institution triggers statutory timing obligations, the Board may deny additional petitions that would complicate meeting the one-year final determination deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exhaustive and equity-focused nature of factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Plastic list is a 'non-exhaustive' set of factors intended to take undue inequities and prejudices to Patent Owner into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may consider other equitable or case-specific factors beyond the listed ones; petitioners should address potential prejudice to Patent Owner when justifying follow-on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve expansion: applicability to different petitioners and relationships between petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Valve, the Board's application of the General Plastic factors is not limited to multiple petitions by the same petitioner; the Board may consider 'any relationship between' different petitioners challenging the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a first-time petitioner can be denied institution if the circumstances (including relationships among petitioners) make additional petitions unfair or inefficient. Joint strategies or related parties should anticipate this scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: §325(d) prior-art overlap concern (Becton, Dickinson factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will consider whether 'the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments previously were presented to the Office' and may deny institution under 35 U.S.C. §325(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition relies on art or arguments that were already considered during prosecution (and meritoriously overcome), the Board is likely to deny institution absent new evidence or a clear explanation of examiner error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: similarities and material differences to art considered during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The similarities and material differences between the asserted art and the prior art involved during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should identify material differences from art considered in prosecution; merely nominal differences are unlikely to warrant institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: cumulative nature of asserted art vs art in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The cumulative nature of the asserted art and the prior art evaluated during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserted art is merely cumulative of art already considered, the Board may decline to revisit the issues absent new rationale or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: extent to which asserted art was evaluated during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the asserted art was evaluated during examination, including whether the prior art was the basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the art was squarely considered and formed the basis for rejections resolved during prosecution, petitioners must explain why reconsideration is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: overlap between examination arguments and petition arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the overlap between the arguments made during examination and the manner in which Petitioner relies on the prior art or Patent Owner distinguishes the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial overlap without new evidence or arguments supports denial under §325(d); petitions should highlight any new factual development or argumentation distinguishing the petition from prosecution history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: whether petitioner points out examiner error
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Petitioner has pointed out sufficiently how the Examiner erred in its evaluation of the asserted prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persuasive showing that the Examiner erred can justify institution even where art was considered during prosecution; provide specific, detailed explanations of examiner error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art factor: additional evidence/facts in petition warranting reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which additional evidence and facts presented in the Petition warrant reconsideration of the prior art or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence (e.g., prior-art publications, declarations) or factual developments strengthen a petition's case against §325(d)-based denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK consideration: overlap with parallel district-court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny institution when instituting review would be an inefficient use of resources because a district-court proceeding is nearing final stages and involves the same claim construction standard, same prior art references, and same arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When district-court litigation on the same issues is advanced, petitioners should evaluate the likelihood that the PTAB will decline institution on efficiency grounds and may consider timing or alternative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Practice Guide principle: one petition sufficient in most situations
rubrics_metrics.description: The July 2019 update notes that 'one petition should be sufficient to challenge the claims of a patent in most situations' and that multiple petitions at or about the same time may burden the Board and Patent Owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should prioritize combining challenges where possible and avoid filing multiple overlapping petitions without strong justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Practice Guide requirement: ranking of petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner should identify a ranking of the petitions in the order in which it wishes the Board to consider the merits, if the Board uses its discretion to institute any of the petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a clear priority ranking helps the Board manage its docket and signals which petition the petitioner considers primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Practice Guide requirement: explanation of differences and materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner should provide a succinct explanation of the differences between the petitions, why the issues addressed by the differences are material, and why the Board should exercise its discretion to institute additional petitions if it identifies one petition that satisfies petitioner's burden under §314(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Succinct, concrete explanations of why each petition raises materially distinct issues increase the likelihood the Board will consider additional petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Practice Guide admonition: limit to one or two petitions; justify 3+
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board indicated that it is 'unlikely that circumstances will arise where three or more petitions by a petitioner with respect to a particular patent will be appropriate' and that petitioners should have clear justification for 3+ petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should strongly consider limiting arguments to one or two petitions; if more are necessary, provide clear, compelling justification for each additional petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip: consider coordination with other potential petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinating timing, strategy, and prior art with other parties interested in challenging a patent can reduce redundant or inconsistent petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination can reduce PTAB burden and avoid serial/duplicative filings, but may increase the risk that parties become real-parties-in-interest or privies and broaden estoppel exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing strategy: file parallel petitions same day to avoid serial label
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple petitions are necessary, filing them on the same day can present them as parallel petitions rather than serial petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel same-day filings avoid several General Plastic timing concerns; if same-day filing is impossible, file in close succession (within a few days) rather than months apart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing strategy: risk of serial petitions—avoid post-denial follow-ons
rubrics_metrics.description: Serial petitions filed after denial on a first petition are particularly unlikely to be granted, because the PTAB views a follow-on petition as unfairly benefiting from what is disclosed in the institution decision for the first petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filing follow-on petitions that appear to rely on the Board's prior institution analysis; if filing after denial, provide strong justification and new material not previously considered.
